## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p falls from 8.09 (N=4000) to 7.542 (N=1M) — overhead amortization at small N, then FLAT. The L1d spill (N≈963) sits below the smallest measured point. The L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680 produces no knee: N=65000 gives 7.622, N=4M gives 7.593. Raising death rate lifts the floor without altering the N-shape: at q=0.25 the curve is flat at ~11.1 ns/p; at q=0.5 it settles at ~13.4 after the N=4000 spike (15.316→13.12). No cache-spill knee appears at any death rate.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 9.02 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 36% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. The algo is overhead/compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound, everywhere. Bandwidth falls monotonically with death rate: 9.02→8.23→7.54→6.12→5.07 GB/s as q goes 0.01→0.5. The transition is driven by death rate, not N — within each q, bandwidth is flat from N=16000 onward. The branchy respawn path (`bl spawn`, PRNG shuffle with `eor`/`ror`/`clz`) costs cycles scaling with q.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized the physics update component-wise within one particle: `ldr q1` loads 16 bytes, `ext.16b v3, v1, v2, #0xc` rearranges components, then `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` operate on 4 float lanes. A gather-like `ld1.s {v2}[1], [x8]` inserts one scalar lane. This is narrow — 4 floats per particle, not across particles. The render pass is entirely scalar: 19 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` perform byte-granular scatter with `csel` clamping. These byte stores cannot stream, capping bandwidth at 36% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — at q=0.01 the algo peaks at 9.02 GB/s = 36% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling, with no cache-spill knee across N. Component-wise auto-vectorization (`fmul.4s` on 4 lanes per particle) is too narrow, and the render pass's 19 `strb` byte-scatter stores dominate, keeping the algo compute/overhead-bound at every death rate.
